chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn Atiyya, from Hisham ibn Ahmar, who said:

I was travelling with Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) in one of the outskirts of Medina when he joined his legs from his mount and fell into prostration, prolonging it and prolonging it. Then he raised his head and rode his mount. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, you have prolonged the prostration.' He said, 'Indeed, I remembered a bounty that Allah had favored me with, so I loved that I should thank my Lord.'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Imam prolong his prostration while traveling?
ai.summary: In this narrative from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) demonstrates the profound Shia emphasis on *shukr* (gratitude) by spontaneously dismounting during travel to perform a prolonged prostration upon recalling a specific divine bounty. This act highlights the scholarly view that gratitude is not merely verbal but requires physical and spiritual embodiment, reinforcing the concept that every blessing warrants a corresponding act of worship. The incident serves as a practical model for believers to maintain constant awareness of God's favors in daily life.
